sampling_model.design: Population identification uses a square fully observed cyclic LiNG model with nondegenerate error coordinates; inference uses an independent observational sample and an explicit matrix-valued FOBI region on the row-scale and permutation quotient.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent draws from one fixed \(q\)-variate equilibrium law.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable in the core identification theorem; a later atomic intervention reveals a matching edge and is the downstream consumer.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The sample covariance whitens the data, the eigensystem of the sample FOBI matrix estimates row directions, \(\widehat V_m\) is the empirical covariance of plug-in normalized-row influence functions, and \(c_{m,1-\alpha}\) is the conditional Gaussian norm quantile. No graph support is assumed known, and all coverage and contraction claims are pointwise.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: LiNG-D outputs the complete distribution-entailment equivalence class and stability selects at most one candidate when the true graph has disjoint cycles.
Distribution-equivalent cyclic LiNG graphs correspond to perfect matchings, their SCCs are invariant, and unfiltered matching samples estimate intervention reward.
The permanent of every nonnegative matrix has a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme.
Counting independent sets is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete even for graphs of maximum degree three.
Unless \(\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}\), no FPRAS counts independent sets on graphs of maximum degree six.
All perfect matchings of a bipartite graph can be enumerated in output-sensitive total time with linear work per matching after preprocessing.
Under bounded eighth moments and distinct kurtoses, the FOBI unmixing estimator has an explicit joint root-sample-size expansion.
Inversion of a sample criterion yields confidence regions for an identified parameter set with consistency and coverage theory.
Discontinuity of a functional prevents nontrivial locally uniform confidence procedures in general.
StableSpIn learns cyclic linear models under the absolute spectral-radius restriction \(\rho(|B|)<1\).

body.tldr: A fully observed cyclic LiNG law identifies a finite monomial row-assignment orbit, but equilibrium stability imposes a global spectral filter on that orbit. The core theorem constructs, from every simple graph \(G\), an explicit rational \(3n\)-variable equation matrix \(W_G\) whose complete stable assignment set is exactly the independent sets of \(G\). This yields \(\#\mathrm P\)-completeness and bounded-degree approximation hardness for the stable count even though the unfiltered assignment count is a permanent with an FPRAS. Exact SCC factorization supplies a local algorithmic fallback, and an explicit matrix-valued symmetrized FOBI region gives pointwise orbit-honest count coverage while contracting to the normalized orbit. The unresolved content is the graph-uniform analytic determinant homotopy that must preserve multiplicities and exclude poles for every intended switch set.

project_justification.gap: Published cyclic-LiNG methods enumerate or sample the full normalized row-assignment fiber and use stability only as a candidate-level screen. They do not classify the complexity of the filtered count or justify transferring permanent-based sampling guarantees after the spectral restriction.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a coefficient-valid realization theorem that controls normalization, signed feedback cancellation, every unintended permutation, and a polynomial-bit spectral margin simultaneously.
project_justification.fill: The proposed rational graph gadget identifies stable assignments with independent sets, transfers exact and approximate counting lower bounds, factors the count over SCCs, and attaches pointwise uncertainty quantification that respects the full ICA orbit.

body.related_work: Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer characterize the complete LiNG-D row-permutation fiber and show that Schur stability can narrow it, but their uniqueness result is confined to disjoint cycles and their discussion leaves efficient stable search open. Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash represent the same ambiguity by perfect matchings, prove SCC invariance, and estimate intervention rewards from unfiltered matching samples; these results provide the setup and the direct consumer rather than a stable-count theorem. Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda provide the FPRAS benchmark for the unfiltered permanent. Greenhill and Sly provide the exact and bounded-degree approximation-hardness donors for independent sets. Uno supplies the alternating-cycle enumeration primitive adapted only after SCC factorization is established. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja supply the FOBI linearization, while Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer motivate region-first inversion and Pfanzagl explains why the final guarantee must remain pointwise at discontinuity boundaries. Misiakos and Püschel study the stronger absolute contractivity constraint \(\rho(|B|)<1\), not counting over normalized ICA assignments.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite exact checks reproduce the complete orbit equality for \(K_2\), \(P_5\), \(C_5\), \(K_{1,4}\), and \(K_5\), with stable counts \(3,13,11,17,6\), but these checks do not prove the universal contour argument. The early kill test is to audit the exact pencil, the inverse-coordinate equations, the \(4gn^2\) perturbation bound, the negative-mode rectangle homotopy, multiplicity preservation, and absence of poles. A sign error, hidden pole, unintended stable permutation, or loss of polynomial-bit margins kills the construction. The enumeration result is output-sensitive in local admissible matchings, not solely in stable outputs.
body.honest_scope: The graph gadget and its determinant homotopy are open and constitute the theorem-level kernel. Conditional on that realization, the counting reductions are standard but must still be written with exact promise and approximation conventions. SCC factorization, pointwise confidence-image coverage, and normalized-orbit contraction are supporting results. Region contraction does not yield singleton count consistency at a discontinuity, and no almost-uniform sampler for the stable orbit, uniform graph-support recovery, or stability-conditioned adaptive-submodularity theorem is claimed. In the acyclic special case every SCC is a singleton and the factorization reduces to the unique LiNGAM row order; when \(G\) is edgeless, Theorem 1 reduces to all \(2^n\) intended local switches being stable, matching \(|\mathcal I(G)|=2^n\).
